rubric:
# Isolated-surface criteria

Assess every supplied unit as its complete frozen isolation boundary and in its
stated actual role. Repeat the frozen role requirement exactly; do not invent,
narrow or replace it, split a legitimately grouped unit, or assume unavailable
surrounding material.

Check coherent English, grammar, technical register, explicit referents, actors,
operations, conditions, comparisons, quantities, units, mappings, scope, actions
and destinations required by that role. Standalone copy must carry its necessary
referents. Contextual headings and genuinely associated groups need not repeat
the whole lesson or every limitation beyond their frozen role requirement.

Judge accessibility meaning from the supplied words and language-neutral
literals, not unseen styling, colors, position, interface chrome or presumed
author intent. An accessible description must state the relationships needed
for its stated purpose; numerical values alone may not explain them.

Give a distinct substantive rationale for every unit. Apply the schema's
severity and verdict rules consistently. Do not infer a suspected correction or
expected outcome from a unit's identifier. A clean pass is valid; do not invent
findings or an expected verdict. Return judgments only, not revised copy.

surfaces.value: For malformed later input, the iterator has already returned the earlier valid document before it encounters the error. A different caller that wrote each returned document immediately would need its own staging to prevent partial publication.

surfaces.value: The handoff to Rust is UTF-8 JSON Lines: one JSON object per physical line. Each object has a nonblank string id and a nonblank string text. Other fields are retained as metadata. For example: {"id":"story-c","text":"A dog runs.","source_group":"family-b"} The document ID is a label, not a token ID or a required filename. The text is still text; tokenization comes next. A newline inside document text must be escaped as \n inside the JSON string, so it does not create a second record. Source and split records remain linked to the exported documents, but a JSONL file alone does not certify that those decisions were made correctly.

surfaces.roleRequirement: Describe the actual fixture/tool/role/reader relationship and the scope needed to understand it without relying on color or visual order. Distinguish document counts from bytes and avoid privacy, completeness or trained-quality guarantees.
surfaces.value: The six-document course fixture passes through NeMo's word-count rule and exact duplicate removal, leaving three documents. A fixed policy assigns known source groups to training, validation and test; Rust loads the exported records. Document counts count those records. Decoded text bytes measure only the UTF-8 size of their text, excluding metadata. Neither quantity certifies privacy, complete related-source discovery or trained-model quality.

surfaces.roleRequirement: Present the retention expression or one defined symbol with the quantities and nonzero-population condition required by its actual explanatory role. Keep documents distinct from bytes/tokens and retention distinct from quality.
surfaces.value: For a nonempty input corpus, the final document-retention fraction is r_{\mathrm{keep}}=\frac{N_{\mathrm{prepared}}}{N_{\mathrm{input}}} Here N_{\mathrm{input}} is the number of input document occurrences, N_{\mathrm{prepared}} is the number remaining after the declared preparation stages, and r_{\mathrm{keep}} is a dimensionless fraction. Neither count is a byte count or token count. With zero input documents, the fraction is undefined; report that condition rather than inventing a zero-quality score.

surfaces.roleRequirement: Present the retention expression or one defined symbol with the quantities and nonzero-population condition required by its actual explanatory role. Keep documents distinct from bytes/tokens and retention distinct from quality.
surfaces.value: In the six-document example, quality filtering retains 4/6 of the original input. Duplicate removal retains 3/4 of its own input: the four records that reached that stage. Their product is the final retention fraction, \frac{4}{6}\cdot\frac{3}{4}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}. Changing the denominator changes the question. Reporting 1/6 as the duplicate stage’s exclusion fraction would use the original input population rather than the 4 records the duplicate stage examined. Keep every stage’s entering and leaving document counts so its fraction can be interpreted locally.

surfaces.roleRequirement: Explain the locally associated external-tool command or operational boundary with its prerequisites, expected result and bounded authority, preserving offline runs and separation from the Rust implementation.
surfaces.value: # Separate NeMo Curator environment This external tool prepares documents. It is not linked into the Rust LLM and does not change the Rust/site Docker image. The thin [Dockerfile](../../docker/nemo-curator.Dockerfile) derives from the official NeMo 26.07 image by digest. The recipe requires its NeMo Curator 1.3.0 APIs. No corpus or model is included in the derived image; inputs and output are mounts.

surfaces.roleRequirement: Explain the locally associated external-tool command or operational boundary with its prerequisites, expected result and bounded authority, preserving offline runs and separation from the Rust implementation.
surfaces.value: ## Run the supplied example Run from the repository root on Linux with Docker, a compatible NVIDIA GPU and driver, and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Image construction can use network access for the official environment. Every runtime command disables networking. ```sh docker build --file docker/nemo-curator.Dockerfile \ --tag learn-llm-nemo-curator:26.07 . mkdir -p .build/corpus/ch41-exact-fixture docker run --rm --network none --gpus all --memory=8g --cpus=2 --shm-size=1g \ --hostname course-nemo --add-host course-nemo:127.0.0.1 \ --mount type=bind,source="$PWD/tools/nemo-curator",target=/course,readonly \ --mount type=bind,source="$PWD/.build/corpus/ch41-exact-fixture",target=/output \ learn-llm-nemo-curator:26.07 /course/prepare_corpus.py \ --input /course/fixtures/raw.jsonl --output /output \ --split-policy /course/fixtures/splits.json ``` The output directory must be empty. Choose a fresh path after an earlier run; never overwrite a completed or failed attempt. The hostname maps local Ray to loopback only; it does not enable outbound connectivity. The actual stage counts for the supplied fixture are 6 input documents, 4 after word-count filtering and 3 after exact duplicate removal. The provided group policy assigns one survivor each to train/validation/test. Decoded text bytes are 11/11/17, 39 across all roles. Either cat-story ID may be retained. `report.json` records configuration, input/output hashes, workflow evidence and scope limitations. All-role `prepared.jsonl` is for inspection; feed `train.jsonl` to tokenizer learning. A role label is not complete related-source or benchmark clearance. The recipe uses NeMo workflows for word-count filtering, exact identification and removal, Pandas for JSONL/table/export operations, standard JSON for the provided split policy and standard hashlib for checksums. It does not acquire data/models, detect all sensitive text or run fuzzy deduplication. Default input limits are 4 MiB and 4096 records. Configured RMM/spill pools are not total device memory admission and do not prove bulk-corpus feasibility. After successful exit, require the report and every file it lists. Each file is written completely before renaming, but publication is not a multi-file crash transaction. Do not adopt an interrupted partial directory. The separately scheduled full-corpus job owns its complete immutable publication and release protocol; the Rust loader does not verify that producer protocol.

surfaces.roleRequirement: Explain the locally associated external-tool command or operational boundary with its prerequisites, expected result and bounded authority, preserving offline runs and separation from the Rust implementation.
surfaces.value: ## Check the helper contract With the same image built, run from the repository root: ```sh docker run --rm --network none \ --mount type=bind,source="$PWD/tools/nemo-curator",target=/course,readonly \ learn-llm-nemo-curator:26.07 -m unittest -v test_prepared_export ``` This selects six tests. They check input limits and the caller-predeclared group join, including unknown groups and prior split metadata. They do not mock or certify a NeMo GPU result. The GPU command above separately exercises the real library path.

surfaces.roleRequirement: Explain the locally associated external-tool command or operational boundary with its prerequisites, expected result and bounded authority, preserving offline runs and separation from the Rust implementation.
surfaces.value: ## Load the prepared training selection With the repository Rust workspace image available, run from the repository root: ```sh COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo run --offline --locked \ -p ch41-corpus-preparation < .build/corpus/ch41-exact-fixture/train.jsonl ``` The summary contains 1 document and 11 decoded UTF-8 text bytes for this fixture. The reader accepts any caller-supplied buffered I/O stream; the file redirect is a demo adapter, not a hardcoded source or destination in the library. The wrapper forwards standard input without allocating a terminal and runs without network.

Use the tool's mature operations and standard input/output libraries, not substitute filters, parsers or deduplicators in the Rust LLM. Use caller-supplied inputs and predeclared policies. The current full-corpus lifecycle plan owns raw-format ingress, near-duplicate/group replay, privacy/rights release, protected evaluation checks and resource admission. Do not lift this example's word range or tiny memory settings into that job without validating the actual dataset and workload.
